Subject: Deployment mode selection & migration plan (post-call recap)

Hi Chris / Ayesha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps based on what we heard: 

Summary of needs:
- Low-latency API for patient-facing triage chat (p50 target ~ 120ms)
- Predictable throughput for scheduled batch jobs (document embedding jobs overnight)
- PHI in transit but encrypted; want SOC2 + customer-managed keys for the production environment
- Current stack: experimenting with another hosted LLM API for POC; some workloads run on an on-prem GPU cluster for sensitive data

Redwood recommendation (short):
- Short-term: Hosted API for fast POC (same API surface, minimal integration effort)
- Pilot/Prod: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) to meet latency & throughput SLOs and keep costs predictable
- Regulated flows: Private VPC with KMS integration for PHI-heavy pipelines or full on-prem if you need air-gapped processing

Migration considerations from your call:
- We can keep POC on Hosted while we provision a Dedicated pool for the triage path (helps compare latency/cost directly)
- For the on-prem cluster migration, our Private deployment supports hybrid routing so you can keep legacy on-prem for certain paths while gradually shifting traffic to Dedicated

Attachments: I attached our Dedicated pricing overview and the security checklist you requested.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Quick follow-up 30m tech sync with Lauren (solutions) to capture traffic shape + KV cache needs — can you do Tue 11/30 or Wed 12/1?
2) If you want a Dedicated pilot, we can provision a small reserved pool (2–4 GPUs) and a short smoke test window — pricing & timeline in the attached PDF.
3) We'll start the security questionnaire; please send the list of required documents (scan, SOC2, KMS requirements).

Let me know which time works and which workloads you want in the Dedicated pilot vs Private.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration plan (tech sync prep)

Hi Chris — good to meet you on the call. Quick technical notes ahead of Wed's sync and answers to your questions: 

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (high level impact):
- Hosted: fastest to start (no infra change). Good for early POC. Limited to our managed model catalog and standard kernel optimizations; not suitable if you require customer-managed KMS or VPC peering.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool in our infra under your tenancy — full throughput control, routing policies, can pin model versions. Supports most custom kernel options via our runtime compatibility layer; we may need to validate your older CUDA stack. Good fit for low-latency, high-throughput production.
- Private VPC / on-prem: customer-managed network and KMS, supports air-gapped or HSM workflows. For on-prem GPU clusters we provide a compatibility shim and migration docs; some very old CUDA/toolchain combinations may need driver updates or a staged container approach.

Migration checklist (short):
1) Traffic profile export (p95/p50, token lengths, batching patterns) — we can help capture this during the pilot.
2) Identify kernels/custom ops used on your on-prem models.
3) Pilot provisioning: we can stand up Dedicated pilot in ~5 business days after contract + infra approval.
4) Data onboarding & KMS setup (Private) — depends on your KMS provider; typically 7–14 business days.
5) Cutover plan: gradual traffic shift with fallback to on-prem for first 48–72 hours.

I'll bring examples of the compatibility shim and a timeline for provisioning to the sync. See attached migration-kickoff-slides for a sample plan.

Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
